source_text:
Ταῦτα μετεγράψατο μὲν Γάϊος ἐκ τῶν Εἰρηναίου συγγραμμάτων, ὃς καὶ συνεπολιτεύσατο τῷ Εἰρηναίῳ, μαθητῇ γεγονότι τοῦ ἁγίου Πολυκάρπου.
οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Εἰρηναῖος, κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ μαρτυρίου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου Πολυκάρπου γενόμενος ἐν Ῥώμῃ, πολλοὺς ἐδίδαξεν: οὗ καὶ πολλὰ συγγράμματα κάλλιστα καὶ ὀρθότατα φέρεται, ἐν οἷς μέμνηται Πολυκάρπου, ὅτι παῤ αὐτοῦ ἔμαθεν, ἱκανῶς τε πᾶσαν αἵρεσιν ἤλεγξεν καὶ τὸν ἐκκλησιαστικὸν κανόνα καὶ καθολικόν, ὡς παρέλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ παρέδωκεν.
λέγει δὲ καὶ τοῦτο: ὅτι συναντήσαντός ποτε τῷ ἁγίῳ Πολυκάρπῳ Μαρκίωνος, ἀφ̓ οὗ οἱ λεγόμενοι Μαρκιωνισταί, καὶ εἰπόντος: Ἐπιγίνωσκε ἡμᾶς, Πολύκαρπε, εἶπεν αὐτὸς τῷ Μαρκίωνι: Ἐπιγινώσκω, ἐπιγινώσκω τὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ σατανᾶ.
καὶ τοῦτο δὲ φέρεται ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Εἰρηναίου συγγράμμασιν, ὅτι ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ὥρᾳ ἐν Σμύρνῃ ἐμαρτύρησεν ὁ Πολύκαρπος, ἤκουσεν φωνὴν ἐν τῇ Ῥωμαίων πόλει ὑπάρχων ὁ Εἰρηναῖος ὡς σάλπιγγος λεγούσης: Πολύκαρπος ἐμαρτύρησεν.
Ἐκ τούτων οὖν, ὡς προλέλεκται, τῶν τοῦ Εἰρηναίου συγγραμμάτων Γάϊος μετεγράψατο, ἐκ δὲ τῶν Γαΐου ἀντιγράφων Ἰσοκράτης ἐν Κορίνθῳ. ἐγὼ δὲ πάλιν Πιόνιος ἐκ τῶν Ἰσοκράτους ἀντιγράφων ἔγραψα κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν τοῦ ἁγίου Πολυκάρπου ζητήσας αὐτά, συναγαγὼν αὐτὰ ἤδη σχεδὸν ἐκ τοῦ χρόνου κεκμηκότα, ἵνα κἀμὲ συναγάγῃ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς μετὰ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἐπουράνιον αὐτοῦ βασιλείαν: ᾧ ἡ δόξα σὺν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
orientation: The epilogue traces the manuscript's transmission from Irenaeus through Gaius, Socrates, Isocrates, and Pionius, and now adds Irenaeus's own testimony about Polycarp and Marcion.
pass_a_gloss: These things Gaius transcribed from the writings of Irenaeus, who also lived with Irenaeus, who had become a disciple of the holy Polycarp. For this Irenaeus, having been in Rome at the time of the martyrdom of the bishop Polycarp, taught many people: of whom also many writings most beautiful and most correct are brought forward, in which he mentions Polycarp, that he learned from him, and he sufficiently refuted every heresy and the ecclesiastical and catholic canon, as he received it from the holy man, and he handed it down. And he says also this: that when Marcion once met the holy Polycarp, from whom the so-called Marcionites come, and said: Recognize us, Polycarp, he himself said to Marcion: I recognize, I recognize the firstborn of Satan. And this also is brought forward in the writings of Irenaeus, that on the day and hour in Smyrna Polycarp was martyred, Irenaeus, being in the city of the Romans, heard a voice as of a trumpet saying: Polycarp has been martyred. From these writings of Irenaeus, therefore, as has been said before, Gaius transcribed, and from the copies of Gaius Isocrates in Corinth. And I, Pionius, again wrote from the copies of Isocrates according to a revelation of the holy Polycarp, having searched them out, having gathered them together already nearly worn out by time, so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me with his elect into his heavenly kingdom: to whom be the glory with the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

choices.why: The verb means to be a fellow citizen or share in a commonwealth; the literal sense is kept rather than a looser 'was associated with.'
Superlative adjectives describing the writings; 'most correct' keeps the sense of doctrinal rightness in ὀρθότατα.
Both adjectives modify κανόνα; 'catholic' follows the glossary decision for καθολικός.
Present imperative; the repetition in Polycarp's reply is kept exactly.
Literal rendering of the famous epithet; no softening.
The glossary requires 'martyr' language for μάρτυς/μαρτύριον; the aorist passive sense is kept.

pass_b_english: Gaius transcribed these things from the writings of Irenaeus. Gaius had lived with Irenaeus, who was a disciple of the holy Polycarp. Irenaeus himself was in Rome at the time of Bishop Polycarp's martyrdom, and he taught many people there. Many of his writings are in circulation, and they are most beautiful and most correct. In them he mentions Polycarp and says that he learned from him. Irenaeus thoroughly refuted every heresy and handed down the rule of faith and the catholic tradition just as he had received it from the holy Polycarp.

Irenaeus also says this: once Marcion, the heretic from whom the so-called Marcionites come, met the holy Polycarp and said, "Recognize us, Polycarp." Polycarp himself answered Marcion, "I recognize you. I recognize the firstborn of Satan."

And this too is found in the writings of Irenaeus: on the very day and hour when Polycarp was martyred in Smyrna, Irenaeus was in the city of Rome and heard a voice like a trumpet saying, "Polycarp has been martyred."

From these writings of Irenaeus, then, as has been said, Gaius transcribed. From the copies of Gaius, Isocrates transcribed in Corinth. And I, Pionius, in turn wrote from the copies of Isocrates. I searched them out according to a revelation of the holy Polycarp, and I gathered them together when they were already nearly worn out by time, so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me with his elect into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory with the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'police captain' for εἰρήναρχος, but συνεπολιτεύσατο means 'shared citizenship/lived with', not a title.
Glossary fixes 'catholic church' for καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία; καθολικόν alone should follow glossary as 'catholic'.
συνεπολιτεύσατο means 'lived with' or 'was fellow-citizen with', not 'shared citizenship with' as modern idiom implies equal status.
Ambiguous 'He' could be Polycarp or Irenaeus; source has Irenaeus as subject continuing from relative clause.

problems.quote: just as he had received it from the holy man
problems.why: τοῦ ἁγίου refers to Polycarp specifically, 'the holy man' is vague; but 'the holy one' or 'the saint' better.
problems.fix: just as he had received it from the holy Polycarp

problems.why: πάλιν modifies whole clause, 'I Pionius wrote again' is odd; 'I Pionius in turn wrote' or 'I too wrote' better.

edits.old: and he shared citizenship with Irenaeus
just as he had received it from the holy man
edits.new: just as he had received it from the holy Polycarp

edits.old: And I, Pionius, wrote again from the copies of Isocrates
edits.new: And I, Pionius, in turn wrote from the copies of Isocrates

fixed: The gloss_edits entry for 'catholic canon' is not a real problem: the English already says 'catholic' and the source καθολικόν is correctly rendered as 'catholic'.
The gloss_edits entry for 'shared citizenship' is fixed by the edit changing it to 'lived with'.

problems.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth from the copies of Gaius.
problems.why: One copy chain names 'Socrates,' the other 'Isocrates' for the same role; reader cannot tell if these are the same person or different.
problems.fix: Note the variant reading or standardize the name with a footnote.

edits.old: From the copies of Gaius, Isocrates transcribed in Corinth.
edits.new: From the copies of Gaius, Isocrates transcribed in Corinth; some copies name Socrates.

fixed: The source names Isocrates in the main text; the variant Socrates appears in the manuscript tradition. The English now notes the variant without changing the main name.

problems.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth
problems.why: Same copyist named two different ways; reader may think they are two different people.
problems.fix: Standardize to one name or note the variant explicitly.

edits.old: From the copies of Gaius, Isocrates transcribed in Corinth; some copies name Socrates.
edits.new: From the copies of Gaius, Isocrates transcribed in Corinth.

fixed: Removed the unsupported variant 'some copies name Socrates'; the source names only Isocrates as the Corinthian copyist.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'catholic church' for καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία; here καθολικόν alone means 'universal' but brief maps to 'catholic'.
last_rejected.ruling: καθολικόν modifies κανόνα; 'catholic canon' is standard rendering, not a glossary-breaking error.

last_rejected.why: συνεπολιτεύσατο means 'shared citizenship/community life', not merely 'lived with'.
last_rejected.fix: who also shared in the civic life of Irenaeus
last_rejected.ruling: συνεπολιτεύσατο includes 'shared civic/community life'; 'lived with' is within acceptable range here.
ἱκανῶς means 'sufficiently/amply'; 'thoroughly' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Ambiguous 'He' could be Gaius or Irenaeus; source clearly Irenaeus.
last_rejected.ruling: Context makes antecedent Irenaeus clear; 'He' is standard pronoun use, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: I recognize you, I recognize the firstborn of Satan
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐπιγινώσκω, ἐπιγινώσκω τὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ σατανᾶ
last_rejected.why: Missing vocative or direct address; Polycarp says 'I recognize [you as] the firstborn of Satan'.
last_rejected.fix: I recognize you—I recognize the firstborn of Satan
last_rejected.ruling: Greek lacks vocative; 'I recognize the firstborn of Satan' is literal and adequate; implied address is clear.

last_rejected.quote: so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me
last_rejected.why: κἀμὲ = 'me too/also me'; 'may also gather me' misplaces 'also', suggesting additional action rather than inclusion of Pionius among others.
last_rejected.fix: so that the Lord Jesus Christ may gather me too
last_rejected.ruling: κἀμὲ = 'me also'; 'may also gather me' correctly conveys inclusion with elect; placement is natural English.

polish.changed: Clarified who is speaking and acting in each sentence, broke long sentences into shorter ones, and made the chain of transcription (Irenaeus to Gaius to Isocrates to Pionius) explicit and easy to follow.

Clarified the copyist chain by using Isocrates consistently, explained the heretic Marcion, and rendered 'ecclesiastical and catholic canon' as 'rule of faith and the catholic tradition' to avoid confusion with the biblical canon.

notes.why: Manuscript variant noted parenthetically, but text then uses both names without clarity; reader cannot tell which is preferred.
notes.fix: Choose one reading and relegate other to footnote.

notes.why: Technical term 'canon' here means rule/tradition, not biblical canon; easily misunderstood.
notes.fix: Note: 'canon' here means authoritative rule of faith, not Bible.

notes.quote: Marcion, from whom the so-called Marcionites come
notes.why: Marcion and Marcionites unexplained for modern reader; major second-century heretic.
notes.fix: Add brief note identifying Marcion as heterodox teacher rejected by mainstream church.

notes.quote: I, Socrates, wrote them in Corinth
notes.why: Section 22 says 'Socrates' then notes manuscripts read 'Isocrates'; epilogus_alius uses 'Isocrates' without note.
notes.fix: Pick one name and note the variant once, or use the same form throughout.

notes.quote: Marcion, from whom the so-called Marcionites come
notes.why: Marcion is named without explanation of who he was or why he matters.
notes.fix: Brief note: Marcion was a 2nd-century heretical teacher who rejected the Old Testament God.

notes.why: 'Canon' here likely means rule of faith, not the biblical canon; modern reader will misread.
notes.fix: Render as 'rule of faith' or add note distinguishing from biblical canon.
